axes.model_access: Open-weights line: two models on record (README verified same day) — F5-TTS (Diffusion Transformer + ConvNeXt V2) and an E2 TTS reproduction; the v1 base model released 2025-03-12; download the weights and run inference locally, no official hosted service.
axes.runtime: Local Python inference stack (conda + PyTorch; NVIDIA CUDA and AMD ROCm install paths on record in the README, ROCm Linux-only); community Gradio Spaces (E2-F5-TTS) exist for trying it out but are not an official hosted product.
axes.local_files: Weights, code and generated audio all stay on your machine; the ModelScope weights page measured 200 direct from mainland (2026-10-30) — the acquisition path works from the mainland; no account or cloud data surface at all.
axes.background: Local batch inference, no task-queue form; inference time varies with hardware and the official line gives no unified latency figure (not verified).
axes.tools: CLI/library usage is the main form (usage examples in the README); zero-shot cloning = give a reference clip + text and synthesize (usage on record); the Sway Sampling inference-time sampling strategy is on record. No hosted API.
axes.context: No session concept — every inference call is independent and carries no state between calls; cross-session memory does not apply (local-model form; context management is entirely up to the caller's own code).
axes.permissions: MIT gives a commercial base (on record via GitHub same day); the model itself performs no consent check on the cloning side — there is no platform-side blocking (a local form has no platform), users carry the consent responsibility themselves (no legal notice on record in the official README, honestly marked unverified).
axes.fit: Fits: local/private Chinese + English TTS and zero-shot cloning research, an MIT commercial base, mainland weight acquisition via ModelScope. Not a fit: wanting an out-of-box hosted API, zero-ops setups, SLAs.

runs:
This site has not completed measured runs. The coding-oriented test protocol is at [protocols/coding/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/coding/_protocol.md) (the coding task suite does not apply to audio products).

**Suggested measurements** (three, all pointing at things the official readable pages do not give):

- **Speaker similarity and stability of Chinese/English zero-shot cloning** (the paper has benchmarks, no third-party re-check; head-to-head against CosyVoice 3.0 in the same scenario is the most informative)
- **Real-time factor on consumer GPUs** (the README gives install paths but no latency figures)
- **Audio-quality gap between the v1 base and the older base** (the 2025-03-12 news says only "better", no comparison table)
unknowns:
- Whether weight-license details match across distributions (HF/ModelScope/Wisemodel, not verified item by item)
- Official legal notices on cloning consent (not on record in the README, honestly marked unverified)
- Training-data composition and licensing (the paper's account not verified item by item)
- Current usability of the Apple Silicon path (the README install section read same day details only the NVIDIA/AMD sections)
related: Also an open-source Chinese + English TTS: CosyVoice is Alibaba's industry-team three-generation line with a training stack; F5-TTS is an academic team's single-repo flow-matching route.
fish audio has a hosted line + voice marketplace; F5-TTS is pure open weights with no hosting.
Same local-inference form as a reference point: Ollama manages LLMs, F5-TTS is the manual equivalent on the TTS side.
